topics.label: Lecture introduction and learning outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer introduces herself, outlines the cancer lecture series, and presents the key learning outcomes regarding environmental exposures, carcinogenicity testing, and tumor initiation versus promotion.

topics.label: Origins of cancer: intrinsic factors, bad luck, and environmental exposures
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics define cancer as an evolutionary genetic disease and evaluate the relative contributions of intrinsic biological bad luck, genetic predisposition, and environmental exposures to overall cancer risk.

topics.label: Mechanisms of carcinogenic agents: initiation, promotion, and host susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the biochemical and cellular mechanisms by which environmental agents drive tumorigenesis through direct mutagenesis, metabolic activation, tumor promotion, and host tissue susceptibility.

topics.label: Methodologies for detecting and testing carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the genomic, epidemiological, in vivo, and in vitro methodologies used to detect carcinogen exposure and evaluate carcinogenic potential.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and risk-benefit evaluation of carcinogens
topics.groupedBecause: The lecturer concludes the lecture by reflecting on daily risk-versus-benefit decisions regarding carcinogen exposure and summarising the key takeaways.
